label: rem:CpBp-sufficient
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:CpBp-sufficient}
Condition~\eqref{eq:CpBp} is sufficient, but not necessary, for the input-coherence property used below. It can be satisfied, for instance, by a second-order low-pass filter, if needed, as a prefilter similar to~\cite{Asada2025}.
head: environment

label: def:concrete-hilbert
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:concrete-hilbert}
Let $\Omega\subset P_{\mathrm{ext}}\times X_{\mathrm{ext}}$ be compact and
let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure with full support on
$\Omega$ (i.e., $\operatorname{supp}\mu=\Omega$). Set $\mathcal H=L^2(\Omega,\mu)$,
with inner product and norm
\[
\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal H}
\coloneqq\int_\Omega fg\,\mathrm d\mu,
\qquad
\|f\|_{\mathcal H}\coloneqq\langle f,f\rangle_{\mathcal H}^{1/2}.
\]
head: environment

label: ass:state-input-compatibility
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:state-input-compatibility}
$C_pp\in U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ for every $(p,x)\in\Omega$.

title: Definition

label: lem:gram-invertible
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For $a\in\mathbb{R}^q$, $a^\top R(\mathbf F)a=\|\sum_i a_if_i\|_{\mathscr H}^2$,
which proves the first claim \cite[Theorem~6.5-1]{kreyszig1978introductory}.
Finite-dimensional subspaces are closed. The projection formula follows
componentwise from the Gram normal equations
\cite[Ch.~3, p.~80]{arbogastbona}.

label: ass:CCK-membership

label: thm:reduced-family
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If every raw lift belongs to $U_p$, set $M=0$ and the conclusion is
immediate. Otherwise, let $j_1$ be the smallest index such that
$\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}}\notin U_p$ and set
\[
\widehat\phi_1
\coloneqq
\frac{\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}}}
{\|\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}}\|_{\mathcal H}}.
\]
Then $V_1=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}}\}$ and
$U_p\cap V_1=\{0\}$.

Suppose inductively that $j_1<\cdots<j_N$ and
$\widehat\phi_1,\dots,\widehat\phi_N$ have been constructed so that
they are orthonormal,
\[
V_N
=
\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}},\dots,\phi_{j_N}^{\mathrm{raw}}\},
\\
U_p\cap V_N=\{0\}.
\]
If every $j>j_N$ satisfies $\phi_j^{\mathrm{raw}}\in U_p\oplus V_N$, the recursion terminates and
we set $M=N$. Otherwise, let $j_{N+1}>j_N$ be the smallest index for
which $\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\notin U_p\oplus V_N$,
and define
\[
\widetilde\phi_{N+1}
\coloneqq
\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}
-
\Pi_{V_N}\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}},
\\
\widehat\phi_{N+1}
\coloneqq
\frac{\widetilde\phi_{N+1}}
{\|\widetilde\phi_{N+1}\|_{\mathcal H}}.
\]
Since $\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\notin V_N$, we have $\widetilde\phi_{N+1}\neq0$. Also, $\widetilde\phi_{N+1}\in V_N^\perp$, so the enlarged family is orthonormal. The new lift is continuous, being a finite combination of raw lifts. Moreover, the induction hypothesis
gives
\[
\Pi_{V_N}\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}
\in
\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}},\dots,\phi_{j_N}^{\mathrm{raw}}\},
\]
and therefore
\[
V_{N+1}
=
\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{j_1}^{\mathrm{raw}},\dots,
       \phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\}.
\]

It remains to verify directness. If $u+v+a\widehat\phi_{N+1}=0,
u\in U_p,\ v\in V_N$, and $a\neq0$, then
$\widehat\phi_{N+1}\in U_p\oplus V_N$. Since
\[
\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}
=
\|\widetilde\phi_{N+1}\|_{\mathcal H}\widehat\phi_{N+1}
+
\Pi_{V_N}\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}},
\]
this would imply
$\phi_{j_{N+1}}^{\mathrm{raw}}\in U_p\oplus V_N$, contradicting the
choice of $j_{N+1}$. Hence $a=0$, and then
$u=-v\in U_p\cap V_N=\{0\}$. Thus
$U_p\cap V_{N+1}=\{0\}$. The nesting
$V_N\subset V_{N+1}$ immediately gives $W_N\subset W_{N+1}$.

If the construction never terminates, set $M=\infty$. If it stops
after $M<\infty$ steps, every selected raw lift belongs to $V_M$,
every skipped index belongs to the space available when it was skipped
and hence to $U_p\oplus V_M$, and every subsequent raw lift belongs to
$U_p\oplus V_M$ by the stopping criterion. This proves
\eqref{eq:finite-M}. A finite $M$ makes the corresponding quotient
finite-dimensional, so an infinite-dimensional quotient forces
$M=\infty$.
head: environment

label: rem:reduced-family-order
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:reduced-family-order}

The finite-order spaces $V_N,W_N$ and their matrices and residuals
depend on the ordering of the raw lifts. This ordering may be chosen
to retain physically useful observables at low orders.
head: environment

label: def:CCK-reduced
title: Definition
head: environment

label: lem:lower-block-exactB
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $k$ and use its defining finite expansion
\[
\widehat\phi_k
=
\sum_{r=1}^{m_k}c_{kr}\phi_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}.
\]
For each raw lift,
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_p\phi_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}(p,x)&=D_u\psi_{n_{kr}}(x,C_pp)C_p,\\
D_x\phi_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}(p,x)&=D_x\psi_{n_{kr}}(x,C_pp).
\end{aligned}
\]
Hence
\[
D_p\phi_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}A_pp
+
D_x\phi_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}f(x,C_pp)
=
\gamma_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}},
\]
and therefore, by linearity,
\[
\widehat\gamma_k
=
\sum_{r=1}^{m_k}c_{kr}\gamma_{n_{kr}}^{\mathrm{raw}}
\]
is continuous on $\Omega$ by the stated regularity assumptions. Moreover,
\[
D_p\widehat\phi_k(p,x)B_p
=
\sum_{r=1}^{m_k}
c_{kr}D_u\psi_{n_{kr}}(x,C_pp)C_pB_p
=
0
\]
by \eqref{eq:CpBp}, proving \eqref{eq:exactB-scalar}.
Stacking gives the claimed Jacobian identity and continuity of
$\boldsymbol\gamma_N$ and $\mathbf\Gamma_N$.
head: environment

label: thm:main-CCK
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The componentwise projection computed above leaves $A_p\bm\pi$
unchanged and has lower-block residual $\mathbf r_N$ by
\eqref{eq:rCCK}. This gives \eqref{eq:Upsilon-split}.
The standing convention makes this identity pointwise on $\Omega$.

Now let $(p(\cdot),x(\cdot),u_a(\cdot))$ satisfy
\eqref{eq:trajectory-CCK}. The upper block is immediate:
\[
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\bm\pi(p(t),x(t))
=
\dot p(t)
=
A_pp(t)+B_pu_a(t)+\delta_p(t).
\]
For the lower block, fix $k\in\{1,\dots,N\}$. Using the canonical
extensions on $\mathcal O$, the chain rule gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}
\widehat\phi_k(p(t),x(t))
&=
D_p\widehat\phi_k(p(t),x(t))\dot p(t)\\
&\quad +D_x\widehat\phi_k(p(t),x(t))\dot x(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
Substitution of~\eqref{eq:trajectory-CCK} and
Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-block-exactB} eliminates the $B_pu_a$ term and gives
\[
\frac{d}{dt}\widehat\phi_k(p,x)
=\widehat\gamma_k(p,x)+D_p\widehat\phi_k(p,x)\delta_p
\]
along the trajectory.
Stacking over $k=1,\dots,N$ yields
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}
\mathbf\Phi_N(p(t),x(t))
=
\boldsymbol\gamma_N(p(t),x(t))
+
\widehat J_N(p(t),x(t))\delta_p(t).
\label{eq:lower-block}
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
Evaluating \eqref{eq:Upsilon-split} along the trajectory identifies
the nominal projected part as $A_N\zeta_N(t)$. Combining the upper
block, the exact input term $B_Nu_a(t)$, and the uncertainty terms
from \eqref{eq:lower-block} proves
\eqref{eq:main-CCK-ODE}--\eqref{eq:Delta}.
head: environment

label: cor:uniform-uncertainty
title: Definition
head: environment

label: rem:weighted-region-dependence
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:weighted-region-dependence}
The definition does not prescribe a particular method for computing or certifying these maxima. The Galerkin closure and residual are determined by the chosen
$(\Omega,\mu)$ and are therefore regional and measure weighted,
whereas the exact actuator blocks $A_p$ and $B_N$ are independent of
this weighting.
head: environment

label: cor:cck-readouts
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
For \textnormal{(i)}, the integral in
\eqref{eq:cck-output-readout} is well defined because $h$ and
$\mathbf Z_N$ are continuous on the compact set $\Omega$ and $\mu$ is
finite, and $R_N$ is invertible as established above.
The definition of $v_{y,N}$ gives
\eqref{eq:cck-output-readout-residual} and
$v_{y,N}\in C(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^{n_y})$. 
For \textnormal{(ii)}, \eqref{eq:state-coordinate-retention} gives
\[
\phi_{k_i}^{\mathrm{raw}}(p,x)
=
\psi_{k_i}(x,C_pp)
=
a_i x_i.
\]
Since $k_i\le j_N$, \eqref{eq:raw-prefix-in-WN} implies
$\phi_{k_i}^{\mathrm{raw}}\in W_N$, and hence $x_i\in W_N$.
Thus $x\in W_N^n$. Since the components of $\mathbf Z_N$
form a basis of $W_N$, Lemma~\ref{thm:general-proj} gives
\[
x
=
\Pi_{W_N^n}x
=
Q(x,\mathbf Z_N)R_N^{-1}\mathbf Z_N
=
H_{x,N}\mathbf Z_N
\]
in $\mathcal H^n$. The standing convention gives
\eqref{eq:exact-state-readout} pointwise on $\Omega$.
Finally, \eqref{eq:exact-augmented-state-readout} follows from
$\bm\pi(p,x)=p$.
head: environment

label: thm:closure-criterion
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \eqref{eq:rCCK}, each residual component has norm
$\operatorname{dist}_{\mathcal H}(\widehat\gamma_k,W_N)$. Summing their squared norms
proves \eqref{eq:best-approx}.
head: environment

label: cor:uniform-closure
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: prop:shaped-residual
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:shaped-residual}
Fix $1\le N\le M$ and the residual $\mathbf r_N$ in
\eqref{eq:rCCK}. Let $F_N$ be a real matrix with $N$ columns such that $F_N\mathbf r_N=0
\quad\text{on }\Omega$. Let $q\coloneqq\dim\ker F_N>0$, and let
$U_N\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times q}$ have orthonormal columns spanning $\ker F_N$. Suppose $S_N=S_N^\top\succ0$ in $\mathbb{R}^{q\times q}$ satisfies
\[
\bigl(U_N^\top\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)\bigr)^\top
S_N^{-1}
\bigl(U_N^\top\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)\bigr)
\le1,
\qquad
\vartheta\in\Omega.
\]
Then, with $D_N\coloneqq U_NS_N^{1/2},
\
\eta_N(\vartheta)
\coloneqq
S_N^{-1/2}U_N^\top\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)$, one has
$\eta_N\in C(\Omega,\mathbb{R}^q)$ and
\[
\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)
=
D_N\eta_N(\vartheta),
\qquad
\|\eta_N(\vartheta)\|_2\le1,
\qquad
\vartheta\in\Omega.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $F_N\mathbf r_N=0$ on $\Omega$,
$\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)\in\ker F_N$ for every
$\vartheta\in\Omega$. Hence $U_NU_N^\top\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)
=
\mathbf r_N(\vartheta),
\
\vartheta\in\Omega$.

Therefore, $D_N\eta_N(\vartheta)
=
U_NU_N^\top\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)
=
\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)$.
The assumed quadratic bound gives
$\|\eta_N(\vartheta)\|_2\le1$ on $\Omega$.
Continuity of $\eta_N$ follows from continuity of $\mathbf r_N$.
head: environment

label: ass:feedback-setting
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:feedback-setting}
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textnormal{(\roman*)}]
\item
$\Omega\subset P\times X$ has nonempty interior, and $f$ and $h$ are
locally Lipschitz on their respective open domains.

\item
The reference $r$ and actuator-realization defect $\delta_p$ are
essentially bounded measurable signals on $[0,\infty)$, with finite
bounds $\bar r,\delta\ge0$ satisfying
\[
\|r(t)\|_2\le\bar r,\\
\|\delta_p(t)\|_2\le\delta
\quad\text{a.e.}
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop:outer-realization
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix a compact interval
$J\subset[0,\tau_{\Omega,N})$. By the definition of the first exit
time,
$(p(t),x(t))\in\Omega
\text{for every }t\in J$.
The components of $\mathbf Z_N$ admit $C^1$ extensions to the open
neighborhood $\mathcal O$ of $\Omega$. Hence, along the locally
absolutely continuous trajectory,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}
\mathbf Z_N(p(t),x(t))
=&
D_p\mathbf Z_N(p(t),x(t))\dot p(t)\\
& +D_x\mathbf Z_N(p(t),x(t))\dot x(t)
\end{aligned}
\]
for almost every $t\in J$.

Using the dynamics
\eqref{eq:actuator}--\eqref{eq:plant-augmented}, the field identity
\eqref{eq:Upsilon-split}, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:lower-block-exactB} gives
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\dot\zeta_N
={}&
A_N\zeta_N+B_Nu_a
+E_{p,N}\delta_p\\
&+
E_{c,N}
\bigl(
\mathbf r_N(p,x)
+\widehat J_N(p,x)\delta_p
\bigr)
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:unscaled-ae-s6}
\end{equation}
a.e. on $J$. For each positive channel scale, define
\[
\begin{aligned}
w_{p,N}(t)&=\delta^{-1}\delta_p,
\quad
w_{v,N}(t)=(\nu_N^\star)^{-1}v_{y,N}(p,x),\\
w_{c,N}(t)&=(\sigma_{c,N}^\star)^{-1}
\bigl[\mathbf r_N(p,x)+\widehat J_N(p,x)\delta_p\bigr].
\end{aligned}
\]
These signals are measurable. The $\delta$ in
Assumption~\ref{ass:feedback-setting}.(ii), with
\eqref{eq:sigma-c-s6} and \eqref{eq:nu-star}, yields
\eqref{eq:normalized-bounds-s6}.

Substitution into \eqref{eq:unscaled-ae-s6} gives the state equation in
\eqref{eq:outer-realization}. Moreover,
\eqref{eq:cck-output-readout-residual} evaluated along the trajectory
gives
\[
y(t)
=
C_{y,N}\zeta_N(t)
+
v_{y,N}(p(t),x(t)),
\]
which yields the output equation in \eqref{eq:outer-realization}. Since $J$ was arbitrary, the
state identity holds almost everywhere on
$[0,\tau_{\Omega,N})$, and the output identity holds throughout that
interval.
head: environment

label: ass:hinf-feasibility
title: Assumption
head: environment

label: thm:lyapunov-are
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Internal stability implies that $A_{\mathrm{cl},N}$ is Hurwitz. Define $T_{\chi w,N}(s)
\coloneqq
(sI-A_{\mathrm{cl},N})^{-1}B_{\mathrm{cl},N}$.

Then $T_{\chi w,N}\in\mathcal{RH}_\infty$. For every
$\varepsilon>0$,
\[
\left\|
\begin{bmatrix}
T_{zw,N}\\
\sqrt{\varepsilon}\,T_{\chi w,N}
\end{bmatrix}
\right\|_\infty^2
\le
\|T_{zw,N}\|_\infty^2
+
\varepsilon\|T_{\chi w,N}\|_\infty^2.
\]
If $T_{\chi w,N}\ne0$, choose
\[
0<\varepsilon_N
<
\frac{
\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}^2-\|T_{zw,N}\|_\infty^2
}{
\|T_{\chi w,N}\|_\infty^2
};
\]
if $T_{\chi w,N}=0$, choose any $\varepsilon_N>0$. Hence the transfer
from $w_N$ to $z_{\varepsilon,N}
\coloneqq
\operatorname{col}\bigl(z_N,\sqrt{\varepsilon_N}\chi_N\bigr)$ has $\mathcal{H}_\infty$ norm strictly below $\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}$.

Since $D_{\mathrm{cl},N}$ is the feedthrough matrix of $T_{zw,N}$,
\[
\|D_{\mathrm{cl},N}\|_{2\to2}
\le
\|T_{zw,N}\|_\infty
<
\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
R_{\gamma,N}
\coloneqq
\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}^2I
-
D_{\mathrm{cl},N}^\top D_{\mathrm{cl},N}
\succ0.
\]
Because $A_{\mathrm{cl},N}$ is Hurwitz,
$(A_{\mathrm{cl},N},B_{\mathrm{cl},N})$ is stabilizable; the augmented
output contains $\sqrt{\varepsilon_N}I$, so detectability is
automatic. The continuous-time strict bounded-real lemma in
Riccati form~\cite[Ch.~12]{ZhouDoyle1998} therefore gives a stabilizing solution
$P_N=P_N^\top\succeq0$ of
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
0={}&
A_{\mathrm{cl},N}^\top P_N
+
P_NA_{\mathrm{cl},N}
+
C_{\mathrm{cl},N}^\top C_{\mathrm{cl},N}
+
\varepsilon_NI\\
&+
\Theta_NR_{\gamma,N}^{-1}\Theta_N^\top,
\end{aligned}
\label{eq:analysis-ARE-s6}
\end{equation}
where $\Theta_N
\coloneqq
P_NB_{\mathrm{cl},N}
+
C_{\mathrm{cl},N}^\top D_{\mathrm{cl},N}$.
Equation~\eqref{eq:analysis-ARE-s6} is a single post-synthesis Riccati
equation for the fixed closed loop.

To verify positive definiteness, let $q\in\ker P_N$. Premultiplying
and postmultiplying \eqref{eq:analysis-ARE-s6} by $q^\top$ and $q$
gives
\[
0
=
\|C_{\mathrm{cl},N}q\|_2^2
+
\varepsilon_N\|q\|_2^2
+
\left\|
R_{\gamma,N}^{-1/2}
D_{\mathrm{cl},N}^\top C_{\mathrm{cl},N}q
\right\|_2^2.
\]
Thus $q=0$, and hence $P_N\succ0$.

Finally, substituting \eqref{eq:analysis-ARE-s6} into the derivative of
\eqref{eq:lyapunov-function-s6} along
\eqref{eq:closed-state-s6} and completing the square yields
\begin{align}
&\dot V_{\mathrm{cl},N}
+
\|z_N\|_2^2
+
\varepsilon_N\|\chi_N\|_2^2
-
\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}^2\|w_N\|_2^2
\notag\\
&\quad=
-\left\|R_{\gamma,N}^{1/2}
\bigl(w_N-R_{\gamma,N}^{-1}\Theta_N^\top\chi_N\bigr)
\right\|_2^2\le0,
\label{eq:square-completion-s6}
\end{align}
which proves \eqref{eq:dissipation-s6}.
head: environment

label: cor:lyapunov-estimates
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Dropping $\|z_N\|_2^2$ from \eqref{eq:dissipation-s6} and using $V_{\mathrm{cl},N}
\le
\lambda_{\max}(P_N)\|\chi_N\|_2^2$ gives
\[
\dot V_{\mathrm{cl},N}
\le
-a_NV_{\mathrm{cl},N}
+
\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}^2m_{w,N}^2
\text{a.e. on }[0,\tau_{\Omega,N}).
\]
Multiplying by $e^{a_Nt}$ and integrating from $0$ to $t$ gives
\eqref{eq:V-bound-s6}.
head: environment

label: thm:preexit-uub
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply the closed-loop embedding above and
Corollary~\ref{cor:lyapunov-estimates}.

Under \eqref{eq:state-coordinate-retention},
Corollary~\ref{cor:cck-readouts}\textnormal{(ii)} gives
$\xi(t)=H_{\xi,N}\zeta_N(t)=C_{\xi,N}\chi_N(t)$
for every $0\le t<\tau_{\Omega,N}$. Since $P_N\succ0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\xi(t)\|_2
&\le
\left\|
C_{\xi,N}P_N^{-1/2}
\right\|_{2\to2}
\|P_N^{1/2}\chi_N(t)\|_2\\
&=
\kappa_{\xi,N}
\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{cl},N}(t)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining this inequality with \eqref{eq:V-bound-s6} proves
\eqref{eq:preexit-state-s6}.

Likewise, \eqref{eq:closed-error-s6} gives, for almost every
$t<\tau_{\Omega,N}$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|e_N(t)\|_2
&\le
\|C_{e,N}P_N^{-1/2}\|_{2\to2}
\|P_N^{1/2}\chi_N(t)\|_2
\\
&\quad +
\|D_{e,N}\|_{2\to2}\|w_N(t)\|_2\\
&\le
\kappa_{e,N}
\sqrt{V_{\mathrm{cl},N}(t)}
+
\|D_{e,N}\|_{2\to2}m_{w,N}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since $e_N=r-y=r-h(x)$, applying \eqref{eq:V-bound-s6} proves
\eqref{eq:preexit-error-s6}.
head: environment

label: thm:regional-completion
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Corollary~\ref{cor:lyapunov-estimates} and
$m_{w,N}\le\bar m_{w,N}$ give $V_{\mathrm{cl},N}(t)\le c_N$
before exit. Under \eqref{eq:containment-s6}, the physical state therefore
remains in a compact subset of $\operatorname{int}\Omega$.
For the auxiliary ellipsoid, the matrix inequality gives
\[
\dot V_{\mathrm{loc},N}\le-\alpha_NV_{\mathrm{loc},N}
+\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_N}\beta_{j,N}b_{j,N}^2.
\]
Integration yields $V_{\mathrm{loc},N}(t)\le c_{\mathrm{loc},N}$, so
$\xi(t)\in H_{f,N}\mathfrak E_{f,N}(c_{\mathrm{loc},N})
\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega$.

For the convolution alternative, variation of constants gives
$|\xi_i(t)|\le d_i$ before exit. The physical state therefore remains
in the compact box $\{\xi:|\xi_i|\le d_i\}\subset\operatorname{int}\Omega$.
In each case, continuity excludes a first exit before $T_{\max,N}$.
Moreover, $P_N\succ0$ and $V_{\mathrm{cl},N}\le c_N$ bound the entire
closed-loop state. The physical state remains in a compact subset of
its open domain, and the exogenous inputs are essentially bounded.
The continuation theorem for locally Lipschitz state equations therefore
gives $T_{\max,N}=\infty$.

The pre-exit estimates now hold for all time. Taking their upper limits
proves \eqref{eq:state-UUB-s6}--\eqref{eq:error-UUB-s6}.
Since $V_{\mathrm{cl},N}\ge\lambda_{\min}(P_N)\|\chi_N\|_2^2$,
the complete state also satisfies
$\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|\chi_N(t)\|_2
\le\gamma_{N,\mathrm a}\bar m_{w,N}/
\sqrt{a_N\lambda_{\min}(P_N)}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The range of $\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}$ is contained in $W_N$, and
linearity is immediate. Moreover,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
&\le
\|R_N^{-1}\|_{2\to2}
\int_\Omega \|Z_N(\vartheta)\|_2\,d\mu(\vartheta)\\
&\quad\cdot
\sup_{\vartheta\in\Omega}\|Z_N(\vartheta)\|_2
\|g\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)},
\end{aligned}
\]
so $\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}$ is bounded.

For $g\in C(\Omega,\mathbb{R})$, Lemma~\ref{thm:general-proj}, applied with
$m=1$, and the integral cross-Gram formula give
\[
\Pi_{W_N}g
=
\left(
\int_\Omega g Z_N^\top\,d\mu
\right)
R_N^{-1}Z_N
=
\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}g
\]
in $\mathcal H$, proving \eqref{eq:Pi-coincides}. For $w\in W_N$, the standing convention therefore gives
\[
\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}w=w
\quad\text{on }\Omega.
\]
Thus $\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}$ is a projection with range $W_N$.

Equation~\eqref{eq:Pi-coincides} and the standing convention identify
the residual components as
\[
\mathcal R_{W_N}\widehat\gamma_k
=
(I-\widetilde\Pi_{W_N})\widehat\gamma_k
\quad\text{on }\Omega.
\]
The standard projection estimate
\cite[Sec.~4.4, Thm.~5, p.~193]{cheney2001analysis} yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
&\|\mathcal R_{W_N}\widehat\gamma_k\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\\
&\quad\le
\|I-\widetilde\Pi_{W_N}\|_{C(\Omega)\to C(\Omega)}
\inf_{w\in W_N}
\|\widehat\gamma_k-w\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}\\
&\quad\le
(1+\Lambda_N)
\inf_{w\in W_N}
\|\widehat\gamma_k-w\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since residuals on $W_N^N$ act componentwise,
$(\mathbf r_N)_k(\vartheta)
=
\bigl(\mathcal R_{W_N}\widehat\gamma_k\bigr)(\vartheta)$ where $\vartheta\in\Omega$,
for $k=1,\dots,N$. Hence, for every $\vartheta\in\Omega$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\mathbf r_N(\vartheta)\|_2^2
&=
\sum_{k=1}^N
\left|
\bigl(\mathcal R_{W_N}\widehat\gamma_k\bigr)(\vartheta)
\right|^2\\
&\le
\sum_{k=1}^N
\|\mathcal R_{W_N}\widehat\gamma_k\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}^2\\
&\le
(1+\Lambda_N)^2
\sum_{k=1}^{N}
\left(
\inf_{w\in W_N}
\|\widehat\gamma_k-w\|_{L^\infty(\Omega)}
\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Taking the maximum over $\vartheta\in\Omega$ and then square roots proves
\eqref{eq:uniform-closure-bound}.
